name: Bright Angel Trail (to 3 Mile Resthouse)
quote: 3 Mile Resthouse 3 6 W/T/E Water available seasonally only. Great turn-a-round point.
why: The park's main corridor trail from the South Rim, down to a resthouse it calls a great turnaround.

name: Bright Angel Trail (to 1.5 Mile Resthouse)
quote: 1.5 Mile Resthouse 1.5 3 W/T/E Water available seasonally only. Good turn-a-round for first time canyon hikers, casual hikers, and late starters.
why: A shorter Bright Angel descent that the park recommends for first-time and casual hikers.

name: Bright Angel Trail (to Havasupai Gardens)
quote: Havasupai Gardens 4.5 9 W/T/E ... Do not go past this point as a SUMMER day hike.
why: A long Bright Angel descent to the shaded oasis that the park names as the summer day-hike limit.

name: Bright Angel Trail (to Plateau Point)
quote: offers day hikes that range in distance up to 12 miles (round trip)
why: The longest Bright Angel day hike, out to a river viewpoint (the PDF lists Plateau Point at 6 mi one way, 12 mi round trip).

name: South Kaibab Trail (to Cedar Ridge)
quote: Cedar Ridge 1.5 3 6120 T Good turn-a-round for first time canyon hikes, casual hikers, and late starters.
why: A steep ridgeline descent with big views that the park calls an ideal day hike.

name: South Kaibab Trail (to Skeleton Point)
quote: Skeleton Point 3 6 5200 ... Do not go past this point as a day hike.
why: The farthest South Kaibab point the park allows for a day hike, with a first view of the river.

name: South Kaibab Trail (to Ooh-Aah Point)
quote: Ooh-Aah Point .9 1.8 6660 Offers a spectacular view. Great day hike.
why: A short, steep descent to the first wide canyon panorama on the South Kaibab Trail.

name: Rim Trail
quote: The Rim Trail stretches from the South Kaibab Trailhead west to Hermits Rest, a distance of approximately thirteen miles (21 km)
why: A mostly paved rim walk linking South Rim viewpoints, which can be shortened with the shuttle.

name: Hermit Trail (to Santa Maria Spring)
quote: The Hermit Trail offers hikes to Santa Maria Spring, 5 miles (round trip)
why: A steep, unmaintained descent below Hermits Rest to a spring, for experienced desert hikers.

name: Hermit Trail (to Dripping Springs)
quote: and Dripping Springs, 7 miles (round trip)
why: A longer Hermit Trail option to an overhang spring, on rougher ground than the corridor trails.

name: Grandview Trail (to Horseshoe Mesa)
quote: The Grandview Trail offers hikes to Coconino Saddle, 2.2 miles (round trip), and Horseshoe Mesa, 6.4 miles (round trip).
why: A very steep old mining trail from Grandview Point down to Horseshoe Mesa.

name: Grandview Trail (to Coconino Saddle)
quote: The Grandview Trail offers hikes to Coconino Saddle, 2.2 miles (round trip)
why: A short but very steep Grandview descent to the first saddle.

name: North Kaibab Trail (to Roaring Springs)
quote: Roaring Springs lies 3,050 feet / 930 m below the canyon rim and is 9.4 miles / 15 km round-trip.
why: An extremely strenuous full-day North Rim descent; the park advises against day-hiking beyond this point.

name: North Kaibab Trail (to Supai Tunnel)
quote: Supai Tunnel (4 miles / 6.5 km round-trip)
why: A shorter descent on the only maintained trail into the canyon from the North Rim.

name: North Kaibab Trail (to Coconino Overlook)
quote: Coconino Overlook (1.5 miles / 2.4 km round-trip)
why: The shortest North Kaibab sampler, down to an overlook.

name: Widforss Trail
quote: 10 mi. / 16 km round-trip; 6 hours approximate round-trip hiking time.
why: A North Rim trail through forest to the canyon edge (closed in 2026).

name: Ken Patrick Trail
quote: 10 mi. / 16 km one-way; 6 hours approximate one-way hiking time.
why: A forest and rim trail from Point Imperial to the North Kaibab trailhead (west part closed in 2026).

name: Uncle Jim Trail
quote: 5.0 mi. / 8.0 km round-trip; 3 hours approximate round-trip hiking time.
why: A forest trail to a point above the North Kaibab switchbacks (closed in 2026).

name: Transept Trail
quote: 3.0 mi. / 4.8 km round-trip; 1.5 hours approximate round-trip hiking time.
why: A rim trail from Grand Canyon Lodge to the North Rim Campground (closed in 2026).

name: Cape Final Trail
quote: 4.0 mi. / 6.4 km round-trip; 2 hours approximate round-trip hiking time.
why: A walk from a dirt parking area to the Cape Final viewpoint.

name: Point Imperial Trail
quote: 4.0 mi. / 6.4 km round-trip; 2 hours approximate round-trip hiking time.
why: An easy trail through the 2000 Outlet Fire burn to the north park boundary.

name: Cliff Springs Trail
quote: 1.0 mi. / 1.6 km round-trip; 1 hour approximate round-trip hiking time.
why: A short walk down a forested ravine to a spring under an overhang near Cape Royal.
